destinations.name: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri
destinations.description: A majestic octagonal sandstone mausoleum rising like a stone lotus in the center of an artificial square lake.

destinations.name: Valmiki National Park & Tiger Reserve
destinations.description: Primeval sal canopy, snow-fed Gandak waters, and Bengal tiger trails nestled against the misty Himalayan borderlands.

destinations.name: Barabar Rock-Cut Caves
destinations.description: India’s oldest surviving rock-cut cave sanctuaries, hewn from sheer granite boulders with glass-like acoustic interiors.

districts.title: 38 ज़िले। 38 पहचानें। अनगिनत कहानियाँ।
districts.subtitle: Every District Has Its Own Soul
districts.description: From the Himalayan sal groves of the north-west to the fertile Kosi marshes, the handlooms of Bhagalpur, and the granite hills of Magadh.
districts.bannerTitle: Discover All 38 Districts in the Interactive Atlas
districts.bannerDesc: Filter by 9 administrative divisions, population, literacy, river basins, and historical eras.

closingCta.headingPart1: Bihar is not a place on a map.
closingCta.description: Embark on a digital pilgrimage across ancient republics, monastic universities, sacred rivers, vibrant courtyards, and thirty-eight living identities.

footer.brandDesc: The Digital Atlas of Bihar. Documenting ancient civilizations, 38 administrative districts, sacred pilgrimage circuits, living folk arts, and gastronomic heritage with precision.
footer.referenceDesc: Data curated from official publications of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Census of India 2011, Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation (BSTDC), and District Gazetteers.

hero.eyebrow: बिहार का डिजिटल सांस्कृतिक एटलस व ऐतिहासिक स्मृति
hero.title: BIHAR 360
hero.hindiTitle: हर ज़िले की अपनी कहानी है।
hero.description: बिहार पवित्र नदियों, अदम्य जनमानस, गौरवशाली धरोहर, पारंपरिक खानपान, लोकपर्वों, प्राचीन भाषाओं व कलाओं की एक जीवंत अमर गाथा है।
hero.scrollPrompt: अन्वेषण के लिए नीचे स्क्रॉल करें

glimpse.title: एक नज़र में बिहार
glimpse.subtitle: बिहार की एक समग्र झलक
glimpse.description: एक सभ्यतागत सातत्य जहाँ नदी तटों पर वैदिक ऋचाएं गूंजती हैं, मिट्टी के चूल्हे सदियों की रसोई संजोते हैं, और आँगन की माटी महिलाओं को दार्शनिक चित्रकार बना देती है।
glimpse.nalandaDesc: जहाँ 10,000 भिक्षु और देश-विदेश के विद्वान खगोलशास्त्र, चिकित्सा, न्याय और चेतना के मर्म को डिकोड करने के लिए नालंदा के विशाल पुस्तकालयों में एकत्र होते थे।
glimpse.littiTitle: अंगीठी और सत्तू भरी लिट्टी चोखा
glimpse.littiDesc: उपलों की धीमी आँच पर पकी और शुद्ध देशी घी में डूबी—सदियों का पारंपरिक आहार जो आज बिहार का गौरव है।
glimpse.mithilaDesc: बाँस की सींकों और कालिख-रंगों से कच्ची दीवारों पर रची गई कला, जो वैदिक संस्कारों और उत्तर बिहार की प्रकृति को अमर बनाती है।
glimpse.valmikiTitle: वाल्मीकि शाल वन एवं गंडक नदी
glimpse.valmikiDesc: जहाँ हिमालय की तलहटी बिहार की माटी को छूती है—रॉयल बंगाल टाइगर और महर्षि वाल्मीकि की प्राचीन तपोभूमि।
glimpse.mungerDesc: जहाँ पतित-पावनी गंगा उत्तर दिशा में मुड़ती है और तट पर प्राचीन ऐतिहासिक दुर्ग रक्षा प्रहरी बनकर खड़ा है।

history.eyebrow: सभ्यता और विचार के ऐतिहासिक युग
history.title: बिहार — समय के पार
history.subtitle: कालचक्र में बिहार
history.visualDesc: यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल जहाँ पवित्र बोधिवृक्ष और सम्राट अशोक द्वारा तीसरी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व स्थापित वज्रासन स्थित है।
history.readMoreBtn: बिहार के इतिहास की यात्रा करें →

epochs.title: वैशाली एवं विश्व का प्रथम गणतंत्र
epochs.hindiTitle: वैशाली एवं विश्व का प्रथम गणतंत्र
epochs.description: लिच्छवियों के नेतृत्व में वैशाली ने विश्व की प्रथम संहिताबद्ध लोकतांत्रिक संसद (संस्थागार) की नींव रखी।

epochs.title: बोधगया में बुद्धत्व एवं महावीर का अहिंसा संदेश
epochs.hindiTitle: बोधगया में बुद्धत्व एवं महावीर का अहिंसा संदेश
epochs.description: गया में बोधिवृक्ष के नीचे सिद्धार्थ गौतम को बुद्धत्व प्राप्त हुआ; भगवान महावीर ने अपरिग्रह व अहिंसा को प्रतिष्ठा दी।

epochs.title: मौर्य साम्राज्य एवं पाटलिपुत्र की आभा
epochs.hindiTitle: मौर्य साम्राज्य एवं पाटलिपुत्र की आभा
epochs.description: चंद्रगुप्त और चाणक्य ने पाटलिपुत्र से भारत का शासन किया; सम्राट अशोक ने युद्ध त्यागकर धम्म के शिलालेख खुदवाए।

epochs.title: नालंदा व विक्रमशिला का विश्व ज्ञान केंद्र
epochs.hindiTitle: नालंदा व विक्रमशिला का विश्व ज्ञान केंद्र
epochs.description: दर्शन, न्याय, चिकित्सा और गणित के वैश्विक विद्यापीठ जिन्होंने सात शताब्दियों तक पूरे एशिया के जिज्ञासुओं का मार्गदर्शन किया।

epochs.title: शेरशाह सूरी एवं सासाराम की वास्तुकला
epochs.hindiTitle: शेरशाह सूरी एवं सासाराम की वास्तुकला
epochs.description: चांदी का "रुपिया" मुद्रा सुधार, ग्रांड ट्रंक रोड का पुनर्निर्माण, और सासाराम में जल के बीच अष्टकोणीय भव्य मकबरे का निर्माण।

epochs.title: चंपारण सत्याग्रह से संपूर्ण क्रांति तक
epochs.hindiTitle: चंपारण सत्याग्रह से जेपी आंदोलन तक
epochs.description: 1917 में महात्मा गांधी ने चंपारण की माटी पर सत्याग्रह का पहला प्रयोग किया; 1974 में जयप्रकाश नारायण ने लोकतंत्र की रक्षा हेतु संपूर्ण क्रांति का बिगुल फूँका।

music.title: सुनिए बिहार को
music.subtitle: बिहार की सुरमयी आवाज़
music.description: चार सहोदर भाषाओं—मैथिली, भोजपुरी, मगही और अंगिका—की मधुर गूंज जो मन्दिरों के प्रांगणों, खलिहानों और पवित्र घाटों पर सदियों से गाई जा रही है।

cuisine.eyebrow: माटी का स्वाद एवं पाक परंपरा
cuisine.title: स्वाद से पहचानिए बिहार
cuisine.subtitle: बिहार का पारंपरिक स्वाद
cuisine.viewAllBtn: बिहार के सभी पारंपरिक व्यंजन देखें

items.name: लिट्टी चोखा
items.description: हाथ से गढ़े गेहूं के गोलों में भुने चने के सत्तू और मसालों का भरावन, गोइठे की आँच पर सिके और गरमागरम देशी घी में तर।

items.name: पवित्र ठेकुआ
items.description: दरदरे गेहूं के आटे, गहरे गुड़, इलायची और सूखे नारियल से काष्ठ के साँचों पर ढले कुरकुरे पावन पकवान।

items.name: मिथिला मखाना
items.description: मिथिला के गहरे कमल पोखरों में पैदा होने वाले मखाने, जिन्हें भूनकर खीर व व्यंजनों में प्रयुक्त किया जाता है।

items.name: सिलाव का खाजा
items.description: बौद्ध काल से सिलाव में शुद्ध घी की पचास से अधिक महीन परतों में बना और चाशनी में भीगा कुरकुरा मिष्ठान्न।

items.name: गया का तिलकुट
items.description: कुटे हुए सफेद तिल और शीतकालीन गन्ने के गुड़ की चाशनी से हाथ से पीट-पीटकर बनाई गई खस्ता पट्टी।

festivals.eyebrow: ऋतु चक्र एवं पंचतत्वों की उपासना
festivals.title: जब बिहार उत्सव बन जाता है
festivals.subtitle: पर्व-त्योहार और लोक परंपराएं
festivals.description: जहाँ प्रकृति पर विजय नहीं, बल्कि उसकी प्रत्यक्ष पूजा की जाती है। बिहार के लोकपर्व सामाजिक बंधनों से परे जल, सूर्य और प्रवासी जीवन के प्रति श्रद्धा का उत्सव हैं।
festivals.chhathTitle: छठ पूजा: सूर्य, जल और प्रकृति की आराधना
festivals.chhathDesc: संसार का एकमात्र वैदिक महापर्व जो अस्ताचलगामी और उदीयमान दोनों सूर्यों को अर्घ्य समर्पित करता है। गंगा, गंडक और कोशी के पावन जल में करोड़ों श्रद्धालु बिना किसी पुरोहित के सीधे सूर्य नारायण की वंदना करते हैं।
festivals.chhathAction: छठ के चारों पावन अनुष्ठान पढ़ें
festivals.sonepurDesc: एशिया का सबसे बड़ा ग्रामीण मेला जहाँ गंडक और गंगा के संगम पर मारवाड़ी घोड़े, लोकनाट्य और श्रद्धालु जुटते हैं।
festivals.samaTitle: सामा-चकेवा: भाई-बहन व प्रवासी पक्षियों का स्नेह
festivals.samaDesc: शीत ऋतु की चांदनी में बहनें मिट्टी की मूर्तियाँ गढ़कर हिमालय से आने वाले प्रवासी पक्षियों के स्वागत में लोकगीत गाती हैं।

arts.title: बिहार की जीवित कला
arts.subtitle: बिहार की लोक कला धरोहर
arts.viewAllBtn: बिहार की सभी लोक कलाएं जानें
arts.mithilaHindi: मिथिला चित्रकला — दीवारों से वैश्विक कैनवास तक
arts.mithilaDesc: कोहबर की कच्ची दीवारों पर बाँस की सींकों और चावल के लेप से उकेरी गई आकृतियाँ। उर्वरता के लिए मछली, सौंदर्य हेतु मयूर और शुचिता का प्रतीक कमल—हर प्रतीक में गहरा दर्शन निहित है।

items.name: मिथिला (मधुबनी) चित्रकला
items.description: बाँस की सींकों और प्राकृतिक रंगों (कचनी व भरनी शैली) से रची जाने वाली वैश्विक ख्याति प्राप्त लोक चित्रकला।

items.name: मंजूषा अंग चित्रकला
items.description: भारत की एकमात्र तीन रंगों (गुलाबी, हरा, पीला) में रची जाने वाली कथात्मक कला, जो बिहुला-विषहरी की अमर गाथा कहती है।

items.name: सुजनी कशीदाकारी
items.description: पुराने वस्त्रों की तहों पर रंगीन धागों के महीन टांकों से ग्रामीण महिलाओं के जीवन, सुख-दुख और सपनों को पिरोया जाता है।

items.name: सिक्की घास शिल्पकला
items.description: नदियों और पोखरों के किनारों पर उगने वाली सुनहरी घास को लाख के रंगों से रंगकर बनाए जाने वाले आकर्षक पात्र व मूर्तियाँ।

people.subtitle: बिहार की वे विभूतियाँ जिन्होंने मानव इतिहास को गढ़ा

thinkers.name: गौतम बुद्ध
thinkers.title: तथागत / बुद्ध
thinkers.quote: शांति अंतर्मन से आती है, इसे बाहर मत खोजो।
thinkers.story: मगध की धरती पर सत्य की खोज की, बोधगया में पीपल वृक्ष के नीचे सम्बोधि प्राप्त की और मध्यम मार्ग का उपदेश दिया जिसने विश्व दर्शन को बदल दिया।

thinkers.name: भगवान महावीर
thinkers.title: 24वें जैन तीर्थंकर
thinkers.quote: समस्त जीवों के प्रति अहिंसा ही परम धर्म है।
thinkers.story: वैशाली गणतंत्र में जन्मे; जिन्होंने सार्वभौमिक अहिंसा, सत्य और अनेकांतवाद के महान सिद्धांतों को मानव जीवन का मार्ग बनाया।

thinkers.name: आर्यभट्ट
thinkers.title: महान खगोलशास्त्री व गणितज्ञ
thinkers.quote: गोल पृथ्वी अपनी धुरी पर घूमती है, जिससे तारे पश्चिम की ओर चलते प्रतीत होते हैं।
thinkers.story: मात्र 23 वर्ष की आयु में पाई (π = 3.1416) का मान दिया, ज्या (साइन) सारणी बनाई और तारेगना से पृथ्वी के घूर्णन को प्रमाणित किया।

thinkers.name: डॉ. राजेन्द्र प्रसाद
thinkers.title: भारत के प्रथम राष्ट्रपति व स्वतंत्रता सेनानी
thinkers.quote: संविधान निर्माण में हमने अपनी प्राचीन सभ्यता की आत्मा को संजोने का प्रयास किया।
thinkers.story: संविधान सभा के अध्यक्ष और स्वतंत्र भारत के प्रथम राष्ट्रपति, जिन्होंने सादगी, विद्वता और निष्ठा से स्वतंत्र राष्ट्र की नींव को सुदृढ़ किया।

places.eyebrow: पवित्र स्थल, तपोवन एवं प्राचीन स्थापत्य
places.title: जहाँ बिहार आपको ले जाता है

places.viewAllBtn: सभी तीर्थ एवं यात्रा परिपथ देखें

destinations.name: नालंदा महाविहार
destinations.description: प्राचीन विश्व के महानतम आवासीय विश्वविद्यालय के लाल ईंटों के खंडहर, जहाँ कभी दस हज़ार विद्वान ज्ञान मीमांसा करते थे।

destinations.name: महाबोधि मंदिर व बोधिवृक्ष
destinations.description: पवित्र बोधिवृक्ष और बलुआ पत्थर का वज्रासन, जहाँ 2,500 वर्ष पूर्व तथागत को बुद्धत्व प्राप्त हुआ था।

destinations.name: कोल्हुआ का अशोक स्तंभ
destinations.description: चुनार के एकाश्म पॉलिशदार बलुआ पत्थर का ऐतिहासिक स्तंभ, जिस पर स्थापित सिंह बुद्ध की अंतिम यात्रा की ओर निहारता है।

destinations.name: शेरशाह सूरी का मकबरा

entities.hindiTitle: भगवान महावीर द्वारा अहिंसा का प्रतिपादन एवं पावापुरी में निर्वाण
entities.subtitle: c. 527 BCE • Apapapuri (Modern Pavapuri), Nalanda District
entities.description: Vardhamana Mahavira, born into the Jnatrika clan of Kundagrama near Vaishali, spent over three decades walking barefoot across Magadha, Anga, and Videha expounding the philosophical tenets of Ahimsa (non-violence), Anekantavada (multi-faceted reality), and Aparigraha. He attained Nirvana at Pavapuri in the palace of King Hastipala.

entities.title: The First Buddhist Council at Sattapani Cave
entities.hindiTitle: सप्तपर्णी गुफा में प्रथम बौद्ध संगीति
entities.subtitle: c. 483 BCE • Sattapani (Saptaparni) Cave, Rajgir
entities.description: Convened immediately following the Mahaparinirvana of the Buddha under the patronage of King Ajatashatru, five hundred senior monks assembled inside the Sattapani cave on Vaibhara Hill. Venerable Upali recited the Vinaya Pitaka (monastic discipline) and Ananda recited the Sutta Pitaka (discourses), creating the foundational oral canon of Buddhism.

entities.title: Establishment of the Imperial Capital at Pataliputra
entities.hindiTitle: पाटलिपुत्र में मौर्य साम्राज्य की स्थापना एवं अर्थशास्त्र
entities.subtitle: c. 322 BCE • Pataliputra (Patna)
entities.description: Overthrowing the Nanda dynasty, Chandragupta Maurya unified the Gangetic plains into an expansive empire administered from Pataliputra. Greek ambassador Megasthenes described the capital as Palibothra: a sprawling city stretched nine miles along the Ganga, enclosed by a wooden palisade with 570 towers and 64 gates.

entities.title: Ashoka Inscribes Pillars of Dhamma Across the Plain
entities.hindiTitle: सम्राट अशोक के धम्म-स्तंभ एवं शिलालेख
entities.subtitle: c. 268 – 232 BCE • Kolhua (Vaishali), Lauriya Nandangarh, Rampurva (Champaran)
entities.description: Following the Kalinga War, Emperor Ashoka renounced conquest by sword (dig-vijaya) in favor of conquest by righteousness (dhamma-vijaya). He quarried monolithic Chunar sandstone shafts, polished them to mirror-like luster, and inscribed Brahmi edicts enforcing non-violence, religious tolerance, and ethical governance.

entities.title: Excavation of the Barabar Caves for the Ajivikas
entities.hindiTitle: अशोक द्वारा आजीवक संतों को बराबर गुफाओं का समर्पण
entities.subtitle: c. 257 – 250 BCE • Barabar Hills, Jehanabad / Gaya District
entities.description: Emperor Ashoka excavated four rock-cut caves (Lomas Rishi, Sudama, Karan Chaupar, and Visva Zopri) into the solid granite of the Barabar Hills as monsoon retreats for ascetics of the heterodox Ajivika sect, demonstrating state patronage across diverse philosophical schools.

entities.title: Aryabhata Authors the Aryabhatiya at Kusumpura
entities.hindiTitle: कुसुमपुर में आर्यभट्ट द्वारा "आर्यभटीय" की रचना
entities.subtitle: 499 CE • Kusumpura (Pataliputra / Taregana)
entities.description: At the age of 23, astronomer and mathematician Aryabhata authored the foundational treatise Aryabhatiya at Kusumpura (Pataliputra). He introduced trigonometry, accurately calculated π (pi) to 3.1416, determined the Earth’s spherical shape and axial rotation, and scientifically explained solar and lunar eclipses.

entities.title: Imperial Patronage Establishes Nalanda Mahavihara
entities.hindiTitle: कुमारगुप्त प्रथम द्वारा नालंदा महाविहार की स्थापना
entities.subtitle: c. 450 CE • Nalanda (Modern Bada Gaon)
entities.description: The monastic university of Nalanda was founded as a Buddhist Mahavihara during the reign of Gupta Emperor Kumaragupta I (referenced as Shakraditya by Xuanzang). Designed as an integrated campus of monasteries and lecture halls, it offered free residential instruction supported by royal endowments from surrounding villages.

entities.title: King Dharmapala Establishes Vikramshila Mahavihara
entities.hindiTitle: सम्राट धर्मपाल द्वारा विक्रमशिला महाविहार की स्थापना
entities.subtitle: c. 783 – 820 CE • Antichak, Bhagalpur District
entities.description: Founded by Pala Emperor Dharmapala atop a bluff overlooking the Ganga, Vikramshila developed into one of Asia’s premier residential centers for advanced study in Buddhist logic (Nyaya), metaphysics, and Tantric philosophy. It housed over one hundred teachers and maintained celebrated scholars including Atisa Dipankara Srijnana.

entities.title: Xuanzang Spends Five Years at Nalanda Mahavihara
entities.hindiTitle: युवान च्वांग (ह्वेनसांग) का नालंदा में अध्ययन एवं अध्यापन
entities.subtitle: 637 – 642 CE • Nalanda Mahavihara
entities.description: Chinese pilgrim and scholar Xuanzang traveled over 10,000 kilometers along the Silk Road to reach Nalanda. He was accepted as a personal disciple by the octogenarian chancellor Shilabhadra, mastering Yogacara philosophy and Sanskrit logic before lecturing and copying hundreds of manuscripts to carry back to Chang’an.

entities.title: Introduction of the Standard Silver Rupiya
entities.hindiTitle: चांदी के मानक "रुपिया" सिक्के का प्रचलन
entities.subtitle: 1540 – 1542 CE • Sasaram and Imperial Mints
entities.description: Sher Shah completely reformed the chaotic medieval monetary system by introducing a tri-metallic currency standard. The core of this system was the Rupiya: a silver coin weighing 178 grains of pure silver (approximately 11.53 grams), alongside the copper Dam and gold Mohur. The term and weight ratio established the direct ancestor of modern Indian currency.

entities.title: Construction of the Monumental Mausoleum at Sasaram
entities.hindiTitle: सासाराम में कृत्रिम झील के मध्य भव्य अष्टकोणीय मकबरे का निर्माण
entities.subtitle: 1540 – 1545 CE • Sasaram, Rohtas District
entities.description: Designed by master builder Aliwal Khan, this 37-meter-high sandstone mausoleum rises from an octagonal stone plinth anchored in the center of an artificial square lake. Combining indigenous pillared chhatris with an immense stone dome that rivals the Gol Gumbaz, it represents the high-water mark of Afghan-Sur architecture in India.

entities.title: Birth of Guru Gobind Singh Ji at Patna
entities.hindiTitle: तख्त श्री पटना साहिब में दशमेश गुरु गोविंद सिंह जी का प्राकट्य
entities.subtitle: December 22, 1666 CE • Patna Sahib (Old Patna City)
entities.description: The tenth Sikh Guru, Gobind Rai (later Guru Gobind Singh Ji), was born in Patna while his father, the ninth Guru Tegh Bahadur, was traveling on a spiritual tour through Assam and Bengal. He spent his early childhood along the banks of the Ganga in Patna before moving to Anandpur Sahib, creating an enduring spiritual bond between Bihar and the Sikh tradition.

entities.title: The Battle of Buxar & Grant of Diwani Rights
entities.hindiTitle: बक्सर का निर्णायक युद्ध एवं दीवानी अधिकारों का हस्तांतरण
entities.subtitle: October 22, 1764 CE • Buxar Plain, Buxar District
entities.description: Forces of the British East India Company under Major Hector Munro defeated the combined armies of Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh, and former Nawab Mir Qasim of Bengal. The resulting 1765 Treaty of Allahabad granted the Company the Diwani (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, inaugurating colonial administrative subjugation.

entities.title: Veer Kunwar Singh Leads the 1857 Resistance
entities.hindiTitle: वीर कुंवर सिंह का 1857 स्वाधीनता संग्राम
entities.subtitle: July 1857 – April 1858 CE • Jagdishpur and Arrah, Bhojpur District
entities.description: When sepoy regiments mutinied at Danapur cantonment on July 25, 1857, they marched to Jagdishpur, where the 80-year-old zamindar Veer Kunwar Singh assumed military leadership. Employing brilliant guerrilla warfare, he liberated Arrah, crossed the Ganga, coordinated with Nana Saheb and Tatya Tope in central India, and recaptured Jagdishpur before succumbing to wounds on April 26, 1858.

entities.title: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917
entities.subtitle: April 1917 CE • Motihari and Bettiah, Champaran
entities.description: Persuaded by local farmer Raj Kumar Shukla at the 1916 Lucknow Congress, Mahatma Gandhi arrived in Champaran to investigate the oppressive Tinkathia system, under which tenant farmers were legally compelled by European planters to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land. Defying colonial magistrate expulsion orders, Gandhi recorded thousands of farmer depositions, compelling the government to pass the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918.

entities.title: Patna Secretariat Firing & Student Martyrdom
entities.hindiTitle: 11 अगस्त 1942: पटना सचिवालय गोलीकांड के अमर शहीद
entities.subtitle: August 11, 1942 CE • Old Secretariat, Patna
entities.description: During the height of the Quit India Movement, a massive non-violent procession of high school and college students marched to the Old Secretariat to hoist the Indian National Flag atop the building. British District Magistrate W.G. Archer ordered police to open fire, killing seven young students while they continuously held the tricolor aloft.

entities.title: Creation of the Province of Bihar and Orissa
entities.hindiTitle: 22 मार्च 1912: बिहार प्रांत का पृथक गठन (बिहार दिवस)
entities.subtitle: March 22, 1912 CE • Patna and Calcutta
entities.description: Following decades of intellectual advocacy led by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha and Mahesh Narayan through publications like The Beharee, King George V issued the royal proclamation separating the non-Bengali territories from the Bengal Presidency. On March 22, 1912, the new Province of Bihar and Orissa came into official administrative existence, celebrated annually as Bihar Diwas.
aliases: New Province of Bihar and Orissa

typedAliases.value: New Province of Bihar and Orissa

keywords: New Province of Bihar and Orissa

entities.title: Dr. Rajendra Prasad Sworn In as First President of India
entities.hindiTitle: डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद स्वतंत्र भारत के प्रथम राष्ट्रपति बने
entities.subtitle: January 26, 1950 CE • Durbar Hall, New Delhi (Origin: Ziradei, Siwan)
entities.description: Dr. Rajendra Prasad of Ziradei (Siwan district), who served as the President of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the Constitution of India, was unanimously elected the first President of the Republic of India on January 26, 1950. He remains the only Indian President to have served two full constitutional terms (1950–1962).

connections.label: Durbar Hall, New Delhi (Origin: Ziradei, Siwan)

entities.title: Jayaprakash Narayan Proclaims Total Revolution
entities.hindiTitle: गांधी मैदान में जयप्रकाश नारायण की "संपूर्ण क्रांति" का आह्वान
entities.subtitle: June 5, 1974 CE • Gandhi Maidan, Patna
entities.description: Before a mammoth gathering of hundreds of thousands at Patna’s Gandhi Maidan, freedom fighter Jayaprakash Narayan proclaimed the call for "Sampoorna Kranti" (Total Revolution), a non-violent mass movement against corruption, democratic backsliding, and authoritarianism. The movement reshaped post-independence Indian politics and established grassroots democratic accountability.

entities.title: International Revival of Nalanda University
entities.hindiTitle: नालंदा अंतरराष्ट्रीय विश्वविद्यालय का ऐतिहासिक पुनरुद्धार
entities.subtitle: 2014 – 2024 CE • Rajgir, Nalanda District
entities.description: Endorsed by the East Asia Summit in 2007 and enacted through Parliament via the Nalanda University Act of 2010, the historic university was reborn as an international postgraduate institution of higher learning in Rajgir, near the ancient ruins. On June 19, 2024, the newly completed 455-acre net-zero sustainable campus was formally inaugurated.

entities.title: Prehistory & Early Archaeology
entities.subtitle: c. 2500 – 1000 BCE (Late Stone Age to Neolithic / Chalcolithic)
entities.description: Archaeologically verified Neolithic and Chalcolithic settlements along the Ganga and its tributaries, characterized by bone tools, microliths, and early agrarian hearths.
aliases: Late Stone Age to Neolithic / Chalcolithic

typedAliases.value: Late Stone Age to Neolithic / Chalcolithic

entities.title: Mahajanapadas & Republican Assemblies
entities.hindiTitle: महाजनपद काल एवं वैशाली का गणतंत्र
entities.subtitle: c. 600 – 400 BCE (Early Historic Period (Second Urbanization))
entities.description: The rise of territorial states and oligarchical clan republics across the eastern Gangetic plain: Magadha south of the Ganga, the Vajji confederacy in the north, and Anga in the east.

entities.title: Buddha, Mahavira & Intellectual Awakening
entities.subtitle: c. 6th – 5th Century BCE (Axial Age of Spiritual & Philosophical Exploration)
entities.description: The philosophical revolution that challenged ritual orthodoxy: Gautama Buddha attained supreme Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya; Lord Mahavira expounded Ahimsa across Magadha and attained Nirvana at Pavapuri.
aliases: Axial Age of Spiritual & Philosophical Exploration

typedAliases.value: Axial Age of Spiritual & Philosophical Exploration

Mahabodhi Temple Complex (UNESCO World Heritage Site, Bodh Gaya)

entities.title: The Mauryan Empire & Ashokan Dhamma
entities.hindiTitle: मौर्य साम्राज्य एवं सम्राट अशोक का धम्म
entities.subtitle: c. 322 – 185 BCE (First Subcontinental Imperial State)
entities.description: Chandragupta Maurya and Chanakya established the first pan-Indian imperial administration centered at Pataliputra; Emperor Ashoka renounced warfare and inscribed moral edicts upon monolithic stone pillars.
keywords: Monolithic Ashokan Pillars & Polished Stone Inscriptions
Earliest Rock-Cut Cave Architecture at Barabar

entities.title: The Imperial Guptas & Classical Sciences
entities.hindiTitle: गुप्त साम्राज्य एवं शास्त्रीय विज्ञान का स्वर्णकाल
entities.subtitle: c. 319 – 550 CE (Classical Indo-Gangetic Era)
entities.description: Imperial consolidation originating in Magadha, marking watershed developments in mathematics and astronomy under Aryabhata, classical stone sculpture, and the founding of Nalanda Mahavihara.
keywords: Foundation Strata of Nalanda Monastery Site 1
Mundeshwari Devi Temple (Kaimur, c. 635 CE inscription)
Sultanganj Colossal Copper Buddha (found in Bhagalpur)

entities.title: The Pala Empire & International Mahaviharas
entities.subtitle: c. 750 – 1161 CE (Golden Age of International Monastic Universities)
entities.description: Under the Pala dynasty, Bihar became the preeminent center of higher learning in Asia: Nalanda reached its zenith, Dharmapala founded Vikramshila, and scholars from China, Korea, and Tibet flocked to study philosophy, logic, and medicine.
aliases: Golden Age of International Monastic Universities

typedAliases.value: Golden Age of International Monastic Universities

keywords: Atisa Dipankara & The Transmission of Buddhism to Tibet
Kurkihar Bronze Hoard (curated in Patna Museum)

entities.title: Sher Shah Suri & The Sur Empire
entities.hindiTitle: शेरशाह सूरी एवं सासाराम की वास्तुकला
entities.subtitle: 1540 – 1545 CE (Administrative & Architectural Pinnacle)
entities.description: Sher Shah Suri ruled from Delhi and Sasaram, instituting administrative breakthroughs: standardizing the silver Rupiya, building the Grand Trunk Road network, establishing the Zabt land revenue system, and commissioning his monumental lake tomb at Sasaram.
keywords: Introduction of the Standard Silver Rupiya (Precursor to Modern Rupee)
Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam) & Sarai Rest-house Network
Tomb of Sher Shah Suri (Sasaram, ASI National Monument)

entities.title: Mughal Subah of Bihar & Azimabad
entities.hindiTitle: मुगल सूबा-ए-बिहार एवं अज़ीमाबाद का वैभव
entities.subtitle: c. 1575 – 1764 CE (Mughal Provincial Era & Azimabad Culture)
entities.description: Akbar constituted Bihar as one of the original 12 subahs (provinces) of the Mughal Empire; Prince Azim-us-Shan developed Patna into the cultural and commercial metropolis of Azimabad; Guru Gobind Singh was born in Patna.
keywords: Raja Man Singh’s Subahdari at Rohtasgarh
Birth of the Tenth Sikh Guru at Patna Sahib
Azimabad Literary, Urdu, and Commercial Renaissance
Man Singh Palace Complex at Rohtasgarh Fort (Rohtas)
Chhoti Dargah of Maner Sharif (Patna District)

entities.title: Colonial Annexation & The 1857 Resistance
entities.subtitle: 1764 – 1858 CE (East India Company Rule & Armed Resistance)
entities.description: The 1764 Battle of Buxar ceded civil revenue rights to the British East India Company; nearly a century later, the 80-year-old chieftain Veer Kunwar Singh led the armed 1857 resistance across Shahabad and central India.

entities.title: Champaran & The Freedom Movement
entities.hindiTitle: चंपारण सत्याग्रह एवं राष्ट्रीय स्वाधीनता आंदोलन
entities.subtitle: 1917 – 1947 CE (The Testing Ground of Satyagraha & Mass Awakening)
entities.description: Mahatma Gandhi launched his first Satyagraha in India in Champaran in 1917 against oppressive European indigo planters; Bihar subsequently emerged as a vanguard of peasant mobilization, Civil Disobedience, and the Quit India uprising.
aliases: The Testing Ground of Satyagraha & Mass Awakening

entities.subtitle: 1912 – 1950 CE (Administrative Separation & The Indian Republic)
entities.description: The administrative emergence of Bihar as a distinct province in 1912, separation from Odisha in 1936, and the swearing-in of Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of the Republic of India in 1950.
keywords: Separation from Bengal Presidency (March 22, 1912 - Bihar Diwas)
Patna High Court & Patna University Establishments (1916 & 1917)
Dr. Rajendra Prasad Elected First President of India

entities.title: Contemporary Bihar: Democracy & Revival
entities.hindiTitle: समकालीन बिहार: जनतंत्र, पुनर्जागरण एवं विकास
entities.subtitle: 1974 – Present (Democratic Renewal & Cultural Revival)
entities.description: The Total Revolution (JP Movement) of 1974 revitalized Indian democracy; the 2000 state bifurcation created Jharkhand; modern Bihar focuses on Nalanda University’s international revival, infrastructural river connectivity, and agricultural heritage protection.

Gangetic Bridge Infrastructure & Cultural Heritage Protections
Gandhi Maidan (Patna, venue of the 1974 historic address)
Digha–Sonpur & Mahatma Gandhi Setu Gangetic Crossings

entities.title: Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama)
entities.subtitle: The Awakened One & Founder of Buddhism • ca. 563/480 – 483/400 BCE
entities.description: Attained supreme enlightenment at Bodh Gaya; preached core philosophies of Ahimsa, Karuna, and the Eightfold Path across Magadha and Vaishali.
keywords: Attained supreme enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya
Preached foundational Mahayana and Theravada discourses at Griddhakuta (Vulture Peak) in Rajgir
Ordained the first order of Buddhist nuns (Bhikkhunis) at Vaishali upon request of Mahapajapati Gotami
Propounded the Four Noble Truths (Chatvari Arya Satyani) and the Noble Eightfold Path (Arya Ashtangika Marga)

entities.title: Lord Mahavira (Vardhamana)
entities.subtitle: 24th Tirthankara of Jainism • Traditional: 599 – 527 BCE / Scholarly: ca. 540 – 468 BCE
entities.description: Codified Jainism, propounded Ahimsa Paramo Dharmah and the revolutionary multi-perspective epistemology of Anekantavada; attained Nirvana at Pawapuri.
keywords: Revived and systematized the eternal philosophical tenets of Jain Dharma
Propounded Ahimsa Paramo Dharmah (Non-violence is the supreme spiritual duty)
Introduced the revolutionary epistemological doctrine of Anekantavada (Many-sided reality) and Syadvada
Attained Mahaparinirvana at Jal Mandir in Pawapuri, an event commemorated on Diwali

entities.title: Aryabhata
entities.subtitle: Father of Indian Astronomy & Mathematics • 476 – 550 CE
entities.description: Calculated Pi (3.1416 as an approximation), proved the diurnal axial rotation of Earth, formulated trigonometry sine tables, and explained eclipses scientifically.
keywords: Calculated the value of Pi (π) to four decimal places (3.1416) and recognized it as an approximation (asanna)
Demonstrated that the Earth is a sphere and rotates on its own axis daily
Provided the scientific explanation of solar and lunar eclipses as planetary and lunar shadows
Formulated early trigonometric tables of sines (jya) and methods for extracting square and cube roots

entities.title: Chanakya (Kautilya / Vishnugupta)
entities.subtitle: Architect of the Maurya Empire & Author of Arthashastra • ca. 375 – 283 BCE
entities.description: Mentored Chandragupta Maurya, defeated the Nanda dynasty, unified the subcontinent against foreign invaders, and authored the Arthashastra.
keywords: Authored the "Arthashastra", the landmark ancient treatise on statecraft, espionage, and economics
Architect of the unified Maurya Empire spanning from modern Afghanistan to the borders of southern India
Formulated the Mandala Theory of interstate diplomacy and the Saptanga theory of state sovereignty

entities.title: Emperor Ashoka The Great
entities.subtitle: Third Mauryan Emperor & Messenger of Dhamma • ca. 304 – 232 BCE (Reign: ca. 268 – 232 BCE)
entities.description: Replaced military conquest with Dhamma; erected inscribed rock edicts and pillars across Asia; established the Lion Capital adopted as India’s National Emblem.
keywords: Inscribed the Ashokan Rock Edicts and Monolithic Pillars across India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Afghanistan
His Lion Capital of Sarnath was adopted as the National Emblem of India, and his Ashoka Chakra adorns the National Flag
Dispatched Buddhist ambassadors including his children Mahendra and Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka and Mediterranean kingdoms
Built 84,000 stupas and endowed the sacred Mahabodhi shrine and Vajrasana in Bodh Gaya

entities.title: Gargi Vachaknavi
entities.subtitle: Vedic Philosopher & Sage of Mithila • ca. 8th – 7th century BCE
entities.description: Celebrated female Vedic scholar of Mithila who cross-examined sage Yajnavalkya on cosmic ontology in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.
keywords: Stood as the prominent female debater in King Janaka’s grand metaphysical congress in Mithila
Author of profound philosophical dialogues immortalized in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad
Celebrated as a Brahmavadini (a woman dedicated to the pursuit of ultimate philosophical truth)

entities.title: Amrapali (Ambapali)
entities.subtitle: Nagarvadhu of Vaishali, Nun & Poet of Therigatha • ca. 500 BCE
entities.description: Patron of the Sangha at Vaishali, gifted Ambapali-vana to Buddha, renounced worldly wealth to become an Arhat nun and author of Therigatha poetry.
keywords: Donated the celebrated Ambapali-vana (Mango Orchard) in Vaishali as a monastery for the Buddha
Authored luminous verses in the Therigatha describing the transient nature of youth and the enduring bliss of Nirvana
Stood as an enduring historical symbol of spiritual autonomy and female dignity in ancient republican Bihar

entities.title: Ubhaya Bharati (Bharti Mandan Mishra)
entities.subtitle: Scholar, Philosopher & Arbiter of the Great Debate • 8th century CE
entities.description: Unmatched 8th-century female scholar from Mithila who refereed the historic Shankaracharya–Mandana Mishra philosophical debate and engaged Shankara on holistic philosophy.
keywords: Presided as supreme referee over the most celebrated philosophical duel in medieval Indian history
Debated Adi Shankaracharya directly on the holistic nature of human knowledge and spiritual life
Honored in Mithila as the embodiment of erudition, fairness, and uncompromising intellectual clarity
Oral philosophical commentaries on Mimamsa and Dharma-Shastras

entities.title: Mahakavi Vidyapati
entities.subtitle: Maithil Kokil (Nightingale of Mithila) • ca. 1352 – 1448 CE
entities.description: Supreme poet of Maithili literature; his devotional lyrics and Nachari songs inspired Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and generations of eastern Indian literature.
keywords: Authored the immortal "Padavali", celebrated across South Asia for lyricism and Bhakti devotion
Created the "Nachari" and "Maheshvani" musical traditions sung at every auspicious Mithila wedding and puja
Authored treatises in Sanskrit, Avahatta, and Maithili including "Kirtilata" and "Purusha Pariksha"

entities.title: Sher Shah Suri (Farid Khan)
entities.subtitle: Founder of Suri Empire & Master Road Builder • 1486 – May 22, 1545
entities.description: Built the 2,500 km Grand Trunk Road, founded the Rupiya currency, instituted equitable land revenue surveys, and built the floating mausoleum at Sasaram.
keywords: Constructed the 2,500 km Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road) from Sonargaon (Bengal) to Peshawar
Introduced the standardized silver coin named "Rupiya", the direct ancestor of modern Indian currency
Constructed the stunning Indo-Islamic octagonal floating mausoleum in the middle of a lake at Sasaram
Standardized Rupiya and Dam currency system

entities.title: Guru Gobind Singh Ji
entities.subtitle: Tenth Sikh Guru & Founder of the Khalsa • December 22, 1666 – October 7, 1708
entities.description: Born at Takht Sri Patna Sahib; founded the Khalsa brotherhood in 1699; warrior-poet who defended liberty of conscience against tyrannical imperial rule.
keywords: Founded the Khalsa brotherhood at Anandpur Sahib in 1699
Conferred eternal spiritual guruship upon the holy scripture Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
Authored the immortal epistle of moral triumph "Zafarnama" addressed to Emperor Aurangzeb
Takht Sri Patna Sahib stands as the sacred pilgrim site of his childhood

entities.title: Babu Veer Kunwar Singh
entities.subtitle: Hero of the 1857 First War of Independence • 1777 – April 26, 1858

entities.title: Chhath Puja (Surya Shashthi)
entities.subtitle: Kartik Shukla Shashthi (October/November) & Chaitra Shukla Shashthi (March/April) • autumn Season
entities.description: Chhath is not a mere ritual; it is a four-day spiritual discipline of self-purification, family solidarity, and deep ecological harmony. The vratis (devotees, predominantly women) undertake a continuous 36-hour waterless fast while maintaining absolute cleanliness. The riverbanks and village ghats become egalitarian sanctuaries where social distinctions dissolve completely as everyone sweeps pathways, carries bamboo dauras, and stands side-by-side in sacred waters.
aliases: The Supreme Mahaparva of Bihar — An Ancient Living Solar Tradition Celebrating Both Setting and Rising Sun

typedAliases.value: The Supreme Mahaparva of Bihar — An Ancient Living Solar Tradition Celebrating Both Setting and Rising Sun

keywords: Day 1 - Nahay-Khay: Devotees bathe in sacred rivers or sanctified water, clean the household meticulously, and prepare a pure vegetarian meal of Kaddu-Bhat (bottle gourd cooked in pure cow ghee and Himalayan rock salt) served with Arwa rice in bronze or earthen utensils.

Day 2 - Kharna (Lohanda): A day-long nirjala (waterless) fast. After sunset, the vrati prepares Rasiya (jaggery kheer made over mango wood fires in a brand-new earthen pot) and ghee-layered rotis. After offering this sacred prasad to the Sun God in solitary silence, the vrati partakes of it and commences an uninterrupted 36-hour fast without water.

Day 3 - Sandhya Arghya: In the golden glow of late afternoon, families accompany the vrati in solemn barefoot processions to river ghats, carrying woven bamboo dauras and brass/bamboo soops loaded with Thekua, sugarcane stalks, coconuts, and wild fruits. Devotees stand waist-deep in the water to offer the first Arghya to the setting sun (Astaachalgami Surya).

Day 4 - Usha Arghya & Parana: Long before dawn, devotees return to the riverbank under starlight. As the crimson rim of the Rising Sun (Usha) breaks across the water, offerings of raw milk and holy river water are made with devotional chants. The 36-hour fast concludes with Parana, drinking holy water and tasting ginger with jaggery.
Thekua (traditional deep-fried cookie of whole wheat flour, jaggery, pure ghee, dry coconut, and crushed cardamom pressed onto carved wooden sanchas)
Kaddu-Bhat (tender bottle gourd cooked with rock salt and cow ghee paired with unpolished rice)
Rasiya (slow-simmered jaggery and milk kheer prepared in clay pots over mango wood flames)
Kasar (sweet roasted rice flour and jaggery laddus made exclusively for Chhath offerings)

entities.title: Sama-Chakeva
entities.subtitle: Kartik Shukla Paksha to Kartik Purnima (November) • autumn Season
entities.description: Sama-Chakeva is rooted in community storytelling, clay craftsmanship, and environmental sensitivity. Women sculpt clay figures of Sama (the female bird), Chakeva (her faithful mate), Charwak, and a wicked slanderous character named Chugla. Each night, girls walk with wicker baskets containing these figures balanced on their heads, placing them in open courtyards under the stars and singing songs of loyalty, sibling love, and bird migrations.
aliases: The Poetic Sister-Brother Folk Festival of Mithila Welcoming Migratory Birds

typedAliases.value: The Poetic Sister-Brother Folk Festival of Mithila Welcoming Migratory Birds

keywords: Clay Sculpting: Young girls dig alluvial clay from local riverbeds or pond banks to hand-model clay figures of Sama, Chakeva, Saptarshi (seven sages), Vrindavan, and Chugla, drying them in the winter sun.

Nightly Courtyard Singing: Under the moonlight, women carry bamboo trays (Dala) bearing the clay birds to community courtyards, sitting in circles singing traditional Maithili songs that celebrate sibling protection.
The Burning of Chugla: On Kartik Purnima night, the cotton moustache of the treacherous Chugla is ceremonially singed with glowing embers to symbolize the defeat of gossip and falsehood.

Pond Immersion & Sibling Blessing: The clay birds are carried in joyful procession to village ponds and immersed, while brothers affectionately crush small clay remnants underfoot to ward off adversity for their sisters.
Chura-Dahi with fresh winter date palm jaggery (Gur)
Mithila winter Tilkut and sesame sweets

entities.title: Gaya Pitrapaksha Mahasangam
entities.subtitle: Bhadrapada Shukla Anant Chaturdashi to Ashwin Krishna Amavasya (September/October) • autumn Season
entities.description: Sanctified in the Mahabharata, Garuda Purana, and Ramayana, Gaya is considered the paramount tirtha for ancestral oblations. The city transforms into an ancient spiritual encampment under the stewardship of the hereditary Gayawal Panda community. Pilgrims systematically visit sacred sites, offering pindas (sanctified rice and sesame balls) while chanting ancient Vedic mantras designed to release ancestral souls from karmic bonds.
aliases: The World’s Oldest and Largest Ancestral Remembrance Pilgrimage

typedAliases.value: The World’s Oldest and Largest Ancestral Remembrance Pilgrimage

keywords: Snan in the Sacred Falgu: Pilgrims take a ritual purification bath in the Falgu River (Antahsalila), whose waters flow beneath the sand bed.
Pind Daan at 45 Ancient Vedis: Offering balls prepared from barley flour, black sesame seeds, honey, milk, and Ganga water at designated historical platforms.
Charan Puja at Vishnupad Mandir: Laying tulsi leaves and pindas directly upon the 40-centimeter bas-relief footprint of Lord Vishnu embedded in solid granite rock.

Sankalp at the Immortal Akshayavat: Concluding the pilgrimage beneath the immortal banyan tree, where legend recounts that Sita Devi blessed the tree for bearing witness to her truthful Pind Daan for King Dasharatha.
Pure Sattvic Pind Daan barley flour and sesame offerings
Gaya Tilkut (beaten white sesame sweet cooked in raw sugar or jaggery)
Gaya Anarsa (coarse rice flour cakes crusted with sesame seeds and stuffed with mawa)
Traditional sattvic bhojan prepared without onion or garlic

entities.title: Sonepur Harihar Kshetra Mela
entities.subtitle: Kartik Purnima (November/December, lasting approximately 30 days) • autumn Season
entities.description: Known locally as the "Chhattar Mela", Sonepur carries millennia of documented history. Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire, historically purchased war elephants and cavalry horses here for his imperial army. Today, while wildlife protection regulations have adapted animal trading, the mela remains a spectacle of rural India, where champion horses, pedigreed bullocks, and camels paraded beside bustling open-air bazaars selling everything from Madhubani paintings to brassware and farming implements.
aliases: Asia’s Largest Rural Cattle, Pastoral & Cultural Carnival

typedAliases.value: Asia’s Largest Rural Cattle, Pastoral & Cultural Carnival

keywords: Kartik Purnima Mahasnan: A sunrise holy dip at the confluence (Sangam) of the holy Ganga and Gandak rivers, believed to wash away sins and bring spiritual merit.
Jalabhisheka at Baba Harihar Nath Temple: Offering holy Sangam water to Lord Harihar Nath—a rare composite deity uniting Lord Vishnu (Hari) and Lord Shiva (Har) in a single idol.
Gajendra Moksha Puja: Commemorative prayer honoring the legendary rescue of the Elephant King from the cosmic crocodile at this very river confluence.
Evening Ganga-Gandak Maha Aarti: Dazzling brass lamp aarti conducted on the river ghats as darkness settles over the fairgrounds.
Gigantic crisp Mela Jalebis made on massive outdoor iron woks
Rustic Litti Chokha roasted over open wood and cow-dung embers
Sweet and spiced Makhana snacks and fresh winter sugarcane juice
Gaja, Khaja, and traditional regional rural confectioneries

entities.title: Makar Sankranti (Til Sakraat)
entities.subtitle: January 14-15 (Poush / Magh transition) • winter Season
entities.description: In Bihar, Makar Sankranti is affectionately called "Til Sakraat" or "Khichdi". The day represents the culimination of winter harvests, welcoming longer days and new agricultural cycles. Families exchange gifts of newly harvested flattened rice (Chura), freshly churned curd (Dahi), and seasonal sesame delicacies. In the evening, the traditional culinary feast of Khichdi is prepared with four classical accompaniments known proverbially: "खिचड़ी के चार यार—दही, पापड़, घी, अचार".
aliases: The Great Harvest Festival of Solar Transition, Tilkut, and Sacred Hot Spring Baths

typedAliases.value: The Great Harvest Festival of Solar Transition, Tilkut, and Sacred Hot Spring Baths

keywords: Ganga & Hot Spring Snan: Thousands bathe at sunrise in the sacred Ganga at Patna, Buxar, and Sultanganj, or in the natural sulfur-rich thermal springs of Brahmakund at Rajgir.
Surya Arghya & Dan: Offering sesame seeds, jaggery, and blankets to the needy as a gesture of gratitude and charity for winter protection.
Dahi-Chura Feast: Midday banquet of thick earthen-pot curd, beaten rice flakes, fresh date-palm or sugarcane jaggery, and sesame tilkut.
Kite Flying & Evening Khichdi: Colorful kites fill winter skies across Patna and Danapur, followed by a dinner of steaming moong-dal Khichdi seasoned with pure ghee and roasted chokha.

Katarni Chura with Mithila or Magadh Dahi in earthen pots

entities.title: Prakash Parv (Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti)
entities.hindiTitle: प्रकाश पर्व (गुरु गोविंद सिंह जी का जन्मोत्सव)
entities.subtitle: Poush Shukla Saptami (December / January) • winter Season
entities.description: During Prakash Parv, the historic neighborhood of Patna Sahib (old Patna City) transforms into a city of lights and devotion. Continuous recitation of Guru Granth Sahib (Akhand Path), daily morning processions (Prabhat Pheris) echoing with cymbals and shabads, and an awe-inspiring Nagar Kirtan with martial Gatka demonstrations wind through decorated city gates. Giant community kitchens (Guru ka Langar) serve warm meals to all visitors 24 hours a day without discrimination.
aliases: The Sacred Birthplace Celebration of the Tenth Sikh Guru at Takht Sri Patna Sahib

typedAliases.value: The Sacred Birthplace Celebration of the Tenth Sikh Guru at Takht Sri Patna Sahib

keywords: Akhand Path: Non-stop 48-hour continuous reading of the holy Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji by devout pathis.
Prabhat Pheri: Early morning devotional walks through narrow historic alleys chanting sacred hymns.
Grand Nagar Kirtan: Colossal ceremonial procession led by the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) guarding the Palki Sahib carrying the holy scripture, accompanied by brass bands and school contingents.
Gatka Martial Displays: Spectacular demonstrations of traditional Sikh martial arts using swords, shields, and wooden sticks.
24/7 Guru Ka Langar: Round-the-clock voluntary community kitchens serving nourishing food to over 100,000 pilgrims daily.
Karah Prasad (sacred semolina/wheat flour halwa prepared with equal parts flour, pure desi ghee, and sugar)
Guru ka Langar (dal makhani, warm rotis, mixed vegetables, and fragrant rice kheer served round the clock)

entities.description: Tens of thousands of monks, nuns, and lay practitioners from Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Tibet, Japan, Vietnam, Bhutan, and around the globe assemble at the UNESCO World Heritage Mahabodhi Temple. Clad in robes of saffron, maroon, and white, devotees carry colorful Buddhist prayer flags, light thousands of butter lamps around the diamond throne (Vajrasana), and engage in silent meditation, sutra chanting, and peace walks.

typedAliases.value: The Thrice-Blessed Day of Birth, Enlightenment, and Mahaparinirvana of the Buddha

keywords: Bodhi Vriksha Puja: Devotees circumambulate the direct descendant of the sacred Bodhi Tree, pouring sanctified water and milk upon its roots and garlanding the stone railing.
World Peace Chanting: Multi-tradition prayer recitations held simultaneously in Pali, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Asian languages inside the Mahabodhi compound.
Ceremonial Procession: Monks carrying the sacred relics of the Buddha in golden urns under ornate satin umbrellas through the streets of Bodh Gaya.
Butter Lamp Illumination: Lighting over 100,000 brass butter lamps and earthen diyas, transforming the temple courtyard into a sea of golden light at twilight.
Sujata Kheer (sweet condensed milk kheer cooked with fragrant rice and cardamom, commemorating the nourishing bowl offered by maiden Sujata)

entities.title: Rajgir Mahotsav & Heritage Festival
entities.subtitle: Last week of November / early December (Annual 3-day festival) • winter Season
entities.description: Initiated in 1986 by Bihar Tourism, Rajgir Mahotsav celebrates the extraordinary syncretic legacy of the ancient royal valley where Lord Buddha delivered many of his most famous discourses and Lord Mahavira attained deep spiritual realizations. The open-air amphitheater is adorned with historic motifs, and the festival features unique traditional events such as horse-drawn carriage (Tonga) races, wrestling bouts (Dangal), and an expansive artisanal Gramshree Mela.
aliases: The Premier Classical Music, Dance & Living Heritage Celebration of Ancient Magadh

typedAliases.value: The Premier Classical Music, Dance & Living Heritage Celebration of Ancient Magadh

keywords: Lighting of the Inaugural Lamp: Ceremonial lamp lighting by cultural dignitaries and state leaders amidst Vedic and Buddhist chants.
Classical Recitals Under the Stars: Evening performances by maestros of Hindustani classical music, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and folk ensembles.
Traditional Tonga Race: Colorful horse-carriage races winding along the scenic foothills of Rajgir.
Heritage Exploration Walks: Curated walking trails to Venuvana Bamboo Grove, Griddhakuta Peak (Vulture Peak), and the Cyclopean Stone Fortifications.
Silao Khaja (hundreds of micro-thin crisp pastry layers sweetened in light sugar syrup, carrying a prestigious GI Tag)

entities.title: Karam / Karma Parva & Nature Worship
entities.hindiTitle: करमा पर्व (प्रकृति एवं भाई-बहन का लोकपर्व)
entities.subtitle: Bhadrapada Shukla Ekadashi (August / September) • monsoon Season
entities.description: During Karma Parva, young women maintain a fast and ceremonially fetch branches of the Karam tree from the nearby forest. The branches are planted in the center of the village courtyard (Akhara) and decorated with wild flowers and germinated grain seedlings (Jawa). Throughout the night, youth dance in rhythmically swaying concentric circles to the beats of Mandar and Dhol drums, singing songs that recount the legend of Karma and Dharma.
aliases: The Sacred Monsoon Folk Festival of Forest Fertility, Karam Tree Worship, and Sibling Love

typedAliases.value: The Sacred Monsoon Folk Festival of Forest Fertility, Karam Tree Worship, and Sibling Love

keywords: Bringing the Karam Branch: Young men and women proceed to the forest singing devotional verses, cutting three branches from a healthy Karam tree with clean cuts that do not touch the bare ground.
Installation in the Village Akhara: The branches are ceremonially planted in the village dancing ground and anointed with vermilion, milk, and flowers.
Jawa Seedling Offerings: Girls offer tender, pale yellow germinated shoots of paddy, barley, and gram (Jawa) grown in bamboo baskets.
Night-long Dancing & Singing: Villagers link arms and dance the Karma folk dance around the branches until dawn breaks, after which the branches are immersed in local streams.
Pitha (steamed rice-flour dumplings stuffed with spiced lentils or sweet jaggery)
Traditional roasted Mahua and seasonal forest snacks
Freshly prepared Arwa rice and country greens (Saag)

entities.title: Sufi Urs of Maner & Bihar Sharif

entities.subtitle: Shawwal / Annual Urs dates (Spring / March-April) • spring Season
entities.description: Bihar holds an illustrious place in medieval Sufism as the heartland of the Firdausiya and Suhrawardi orders. The architectural wonder of Chhoti Dargah at Maner, completed in 1616 with magnificent carved Chunar sandstone and a 50-foot dome over a tranquil tank, hosts an annual Urs where thousands assemble. The atmosphere is one of profound peace, where boundaries of caste and religion evaporate in shared devotional ecstasy and the distribution of the famous Maner ka Laddoo.
aliases: The 700-Year-Old Syncretic Sufi Pilgrimage and Qawwali Tradition of Bihar

typedAliases.value: The 700-Year-Old Syncretic Sufi Pilgrimage and Qawwali Tradition of Bihar

keywords: Ghusl & Sandalwood Rite: Ceremonial washing and anointing of the sacred tomb with pure rose water and sandalwood paste.
Chadar Poshi Procession: Carrying large embroidered green and gold satin sheets accompanied by Sufi tambourines and naat poetry.
Mehfil-e-Sama (Qawwali Night): Devotional singing by hereditary qawwals tracing centuries of mystic Persian, Urdu, and Bhojpuri verses of divine love.
Langar & Tabarruk: Mass distribution of sweet delicacies and wholesome meals to all visiting pilgrims regardless of background.
Maner ka Motichoor Laddoo (historic ghee-fried tiny gram-flour pearls flavored with saffron and cardamom, made with local sweet well water)
Traditional Sheer Khurma and Zarda Pulao
