entities.title: Mithila Vivah Panchami
entities.subtitle: Margashirsha Shukla Panchami (November / December) • winter Season
entities.description: During Vivah Panchami, courtyards and temple verandas across Madhubani and Sitamarhi are washed and decorated with intricate rice-paste Aripan floor paintings. Women gather in colorful traditional sarees to perform traditional Maithili marriage rituals: singing humorous welcoming songs (Gali geet), presenting wedding trays with paan and makhana, and re-enacting the Jaimala garland exchange with festive jubilation.
aliases: The Living Folk Celebration Welcoming Lord Rama as the Beloved Son-in-Law of Mithila

typedAliases.value: The Living Folk Celebration Welcoming Lord Rama as the Beloved Son-in-Law of Mithila

keywords: Aripan Floor Art: Women draw auspicious geometric white rice-powder motifs (Swastik, Shankha, Lotus) in courtyards for wedding blessings.
Baraat Re-enactment: Colorfully decorated processions carrying decorated palanquins, brass lamps, and music through village lanes.
Kohbar & Jaimala Ceremony: Symbolic exchange of flower garlands in front of elaborately painted Kohbar folk murals.
Maithili Wedding Singing: Women sing traditional songs such as Samdaun, Sohar, and humorous teasing verses welcoming the Ayodhya procession.
Makhana Kheer (slow-cooked foxnut and milk pudding topped with roasted almonds)
Tarua (assorted seasonal vegetables dipped in spiced rice-gram batter and crisp-fried in mustard oil)
Traditional Til Sankranti sweets and freshly harvested seasonal winter crops

connections.label: Mithila Vivah Geet: Samdaun (Bar Re Jatan Se Hum)
connections.hindiLabel: मिथिला समदौन: बड़ रे जतन से हम (बेटी विदाई गीत)

entities.title: Litti Chokha
entities.subtitle: bhojpur • Staple & Main Course
entities.description: Whole-wheat dough balls filled with roasted gram flour (sattu) spiced with carom, nigella seeds, garlic, and pickled mustard oil, traditionally baked over dying cow-dung cake or wood embers, then cracked open and submerged in pure desi ghee, served with smoky mashed eggplant and tomato chokha.
keywords: Kachhi ghani mustard oil & lemon juice
Pickled red chili masala (Bharwa mirch ka masala)
Boiled potatoes, raw garlic juliennes, and green chilies

connections.label: Imperial Echoes: The Mauryan & Guptan Capitals
connections.hindiLabel: मौर्य साम्राज्य की गूँज: पाटलिपुत्र से बराबर तक

entities.title: Thekua (Khajuria / Thokwa)
entities.subtitle: patna • Ritual Offering / Sacred Sweet
entities.description: The sacred, traditional Prasad of Chhath Puja. A dense, crisp-crusted sweet made from coarse stone-milled wheat flour, unrefined dark sugarcane jaggery (gur), pure cow ghee, coconut slivers, and green cardamom, pressed onto carved wooden molds.
keywords: Coarsely stone-milled whole wheat flour (Mota Atta)
Dark country jaggery (Gur) dissolved in water
Desi cow ghee for dough shortening (Moyen)
Desi ghee or pure oil for slow deep-frying

entities.title: Champaran Ahuna (Handi) Mutton
entities.subtitle: east-champaran • Staple & Main Course
entities.description: A slow-cooked mutton preparation from Champaran, closely associated with Ghorasahan, Motihari, and Bettiah. Tender goat meat marinated with sliced onions, raw mustard oil, whole spices, and entire intact bulbs of garlic, sealed inside an unglazed clay handi with wheat dough and simmered over embers.
keywords: Fresh goat meat on the bone
Thinly sliced red onions (equal in weight to meat)
Whole crushed spices: black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves
Freshly ground dry red chilies and black pepper
Wheat flour dough for sealing handi neck

entities.title: Silao Ka Khaja
entities.subtitle: nalanda • Sweet & Confection (GI Tagged)
entities.description: A multi-layered, delicate crispy confection from the historic village of Silao, situated between Rajgir and Nalanda. Awarded the Geographical Indication (GI) tag for its distinctive flaky stratification and light sweetness.
keywords: Sugar syrup infused with green cardamom

entities.title: Gaya Tilkut
entities.subtitle: gaya • Seasonal Sweet
entities.description: A winter specialty from the narrow lanes of Ramna in Gaya. Roasted white sesame seeds combined with pulled jaggery or sugar syrup, rhythmically hand-pounded with heavy wooden mallets until it forms a brittle, feather-light, melt-in-the-mouth wafer.
keywords: Cleaned and roasted white sesame seeds (Safed Til)
Winter sugarcane jaggery (Gur) or refined sugar syrup

connections.label: The Awakening Trail: Following the Buddha's Footsteps
connections.hindiLabel: बोधिसत्व पथ: भगवान बुद्ध के पदचिह्न

entities.title: Mithila Makhana Kheer
entities.subtitle: madhubani • Dessert & Sacred Offering
entities.description: A slow-simmered dessert of Mithila prepared from GI-tagged Mithila Makhana (Application No. 696). Popped gorgon seeds are toasted in ghee, partially crushed to thicken whole milk, and flavored with saffron, cardamom, and roasted dry fruits.
keywords: Cashews and almonds lightly toasted in pure cow ghee

connections.label: Mithila: Sacred Waters, Poetry & Living Art
connections.hindiLabel: मिथिला: पावन पोखरि, विद्यापति की कविता और जीवंत कला

entities.title: Dal Pitha (Bagia / Bhakosa)
entities.subtitle: muzaffarpur • Breakfast & Winter Staple
entities.description: Steamed dumplings made from rice flour dough, stuffed with a coarse mixture of soaked chana dal (Bengal gram), fresh garlic, green chilies, cumin seeds, and asafoetida. Known as Bagia in Mithila and Bhakosa/Pitha across Tirhut and Bhojpur.
keywords: Fresh garlic cloves, green chilies, and ginger
Turmeric, freshly chopped coriander, and salt

entities.title: Sattu Sharbat (Namkeen & Meetha)
entities.subtitle: bhojpur • Traditional Beverage & Sustenance
entities.description: A traditional beverage of Bihar made from stone-ground roasted gram flour (chana sattu) dissolved in earthen-pitcher water, served either savory with roasted cumin, black salt, green chili, and lemon, or sweet with crushed country jaggery.
keywords: Pure chana sattu (roasted Bengal gram flour)
Black salt (Kala namak) & roasted cumin powder (Bhuna jeera)
Finely chopped green chilies, mint leaves, and red onion (optional)
Or dark sugarcane jaggery (for meetha version)

entities.title: Dahi Chura
entities.subtitle: patna • Breakfast & Ritual Staple
entities.description: A harvest meal combining beaten flattened rice (chura) with clay-pot set curd (dahi), sweetened with winter jaggery or accompanied by roasted tilkut and a side of potato-cauliflower subzi or pickled chili.
keywords: Aromatic flattened rice (Katarani or local Chura)
Dark country jaggery (Gur) or cane sugar
Savory accompaniment: Aloo Gobhi subzi or red stuffed pickle

connections.label: Mithila: Sacred Waters, Poetry & Living Art
connections.hindiLabel: मिथिला: पावन पोखरि, विद्यापति की कविता और जीवंत कला

entities.title: Bihari Malpua
entities.subtitle: patna • Festive Sweet
entities.description: A festive sweet pancake prepared during Holi and celebratory gatherings. Made from a batter of wheat flour, mashed ripe bananas, milk, crushed green cardamom, and fennel seeds, fried gently in desi ghee and soaked in warm cardamom sugar syrup.

entities.title: Gaya Anarsa
entities.subtitle: gaya • Traditional Confection
entities.description: A traditional rice-based sweet confection crafted in the lanes of Gaya. Made from aged rice soaked for days, powdered, mixed with jaggery or sugar into a pliable dough, stuffed with mawa (khoya) flavored with cardamom, coated with white sesame seeds, and fried to golden perfection.
keywords: Aged rice soaked for 3 days and shade-dried
Dark country jaggery (Gur) or fine sugar
Mawa (khoya) mixed with cardamom powder for filling
White sesame seeds (Safed Til) for crust

entities.title: Bihari Khichdi & Chokha
entities.subtitle: patna • Ritual Staple & Comfort Food
entities.description: The traditional Saturday and Makar Sankranti meal of Bihar. A pot of rice and roasted moong or urad dal, tempered with whole cumin, asafoetida, and dry red chilies, traditionally accompanied by the "Chaar Yaar" (Four Friends): Chokha, Papad, Ghee, and Achar.
keywords: Dry-roasted yellow moong dal or split urad dal
Chaar Yaar: Roasted potato/eggplant chokha, papad, desi ghee, and spicy mango/chili pickle

entities.title: Runni Saidpur Balushahi
entities.subtitle: sitamarhi • Sweet & Confection
entities.description: A celebrated confection from the wayside sweet-makers of Runni Saidpur on the Muzaffarpur-Sitamarhi highway. Golden, multi-laminated discs with a flaky, micro-creviced texture that absorbs warm sugar syrup while maintaining a delicate crystalline crust.
keywords: Fresh curd (Dahi) & a pinch of baking soda
Warm sugar syrup scented with saffron and cardamom

entities.title: Bihari Chana Ghugni
entities.subtitle: patna • Snack & Breakfast
entities.description: A spiced, semi-dry brown chickpea curry tempered with cumin, whole dried red chilies, ginger juliennes, and amchur (dry mango powder), served alongside flattened beaten rice (Chura) or hot puffed puris.
keywords: Kala chana (small brown chickpeas) soaked overnight
Finely sliced red onions, tomatoes, ginger, and garlic
Roasted cumin powder, coriander, and amchur powder
Fresh green chilies and julienned ginger for garnish

entities.title: Sattu Makuni (Stuffed Paratha)
entities.subtitle: bhojpur • Staple & Main Course
entities.description: A pan-roasted whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced sattu. The dough is rolled thin and roasted on an iron tawa with drops of mustard oil or ghee until blistered and golden, eaten alongside baingan chokha or tangy mango pickle.
keywords: Minced garlic, green chilies, and fresh coriander
Ghee or mustard oil for tawa roasting

entities.title: Mithila Machh Bhaat
entities.subtitle: madhubani • Staple & Main Course
entities.description: Freshwater pond fish (such as Rohu or Catla) cooked in a pungent golden mustard-seed, turmeric, and dried mango (amchur) gravy, paired with hot steamed fine rice (bhaat). A cornerstone of Maithil festive and domestic hospitality.
keywords: Fresh freshwater river/pond fish cutlets (Rohu / Katla)
Yellow and black mustard seeds ground to fine paste (Sorse baata)
Pure mustard oil for shallow frying and gravy
Panch phoron (five-spice blend) & whole green chilies
Turmeric, coriander powder, and amchur (dry mango powder)

entities.title: Maithili
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Eastern group / Bihari branch) • Script: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Tirhuta (ceremonial and calligraphic)
entities.description: Maithili is the literary and cultural language of the Mithila region of northern Bihar and southeastern Nepal. Endowed with a written literary heritage dating from at least the 14th century, it was incorporated into the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India in 2003 (92nd Constitutional Amendment Act).
aliases: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Tirhuta (ceremonial and calligraphic)

typedAliases.value: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Tirhuta (ceremonial and calligraphic)

connections.label: Mithila Vivah Geet: Samdaun (Bar Re Jatan Se Hum)
connections.hindiLabel: मिथिला समदौन: बड़ रे जतन से हम (बेटी विदाई गीत)

connections.label: Jai Jai Bhairavi (Vidyapati Gosaunik Geet)
connections.hindiLabel: जय जय भैरवी असुर भयावनि (विद्यापति नचारी)

entities.title: Bhojpuri
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Eastern group / Bihari branch) • Script: Devanagari (predominant today); Kaithi (historical legal and mercantile script)
entities.description: Bhojpuri is a major Indo-Aryan language spoken across western Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh, and the Terai of Nepal. Renowned for its theatrical traditions, vibrant folk songs, and the historical literature of migration, it holds deep cultural resonance across northern India and the global Indian diaspora.
aliases: Devanagari (predominant today); Kaithi (historical legal and mercantile script)

typedAliases.value: Devanagari (predominant today); Kaithi (historical legal and mercantile script)

connections.label: Kelwa Ke Paat Par (Ugeelan Surujmal)
connections.hindiLabel: केलवा के पात पर उगेलन सुरुजमल

connections.label: Kaanch Hi Baans Ke Bahangiya
connections.hindiLabel: काँच ही बाँस के बहँगिया

entities.title: Magahi
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Eastern group / Bihari branch) • Script: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Kaithi (historical manuscripts and revenue records)
entities.description: Magahi is the native language of the central Magadh region south of the Ganga. Carrying memories of Rajgir, Bodh Gaya, and ancient Pataliputra, it is celebrated for its warm, direct idioms, heroic oral epics like Lorikayan, and rich lifecycle folklore.
aliases: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Kaithi (historical manuscripts and revenue records)

typedAliases.value: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Kaithi (historical manuscripts and revenue records)

connections.label: Bhojpuri & Magahi Sohar Geet
connections.hindiLabel: सोहर गीत (संस्कार एवं जन्मोत्सव)

connections.label: Kabir Nirgun: Hans Akela (Udd Jayega Hans Akela)
connections.hindiLabel: कबीर निर्गुण: उड़ जाएगा हंस अकेला

entities.title: Angika
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Eastern group / Bihari branch) • Script: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Kaithi (historical usage)
entities.description: Angika is the native speech variety of the eastern Anga region of Bihar. Bound to the riverine bends of the Ganga near Sultanganj and Bhagalpur, it possesses a celebrated oral ballad tradition centered around the serpent goddess Bishahari and the chaste heroine Behula.
aliases: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Kaithi (historical usage)

typedAliases.value: Devanagari (predominant in modern printing); Kaithi (historical usage)

connections.label: Bihula Bishahari Angika Geet (Bishahari Maiya Khola Na He Kewar)
connections.hindiLabel: बिहुला विषहरी अंगिका लोकगीत: विषहरी मईया खोला ना हे केवार

entities.title: Bajjika
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Eastern group / Transitional variety) • Script: Devanagari
entities.description: Bajjika is the speech variety of the historic Licchavi republic region (Vaishali, Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, and Sheohar). Named after the ancient Vajjian confederacy, it is characterized by its gentle cadence, unique pronoun system, and rich repertoire of rural folktales.

entities.title: Urdu
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Central group / Hindustani standard with Perso-Arabic vocabulary) • Script: Perso-Arabic (Nastaliq script)
entities.description: Urdu is the second official language of Bihar, recognized in 1980 under the Bihar Official Language (Amendment) Act—making Bihar the first Indian state to accord Urdu official status. Bihar has produced legendary Urdu poets, freedom fighters, and institutions such as the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library.
keywords: Indo-Aryan (Central group / Hindustani standard with Perso-Arabic vocabulary)

connections.label: Maner Sharif Urs Celebration & Qawwali
connections.hindiLabel: मनेर शरीफ उर्स कव्वाली परंपरा

entities.title: Surjapuri
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Eastern group / Kamatapuri-Maithili transition) • Script: Devanagari
entities.description: Surjapuri is the everyday mother tongue of the northeastern borderlands of Bihar along the Mahananda river basin. Reflecting the historical interactions of Bihar, Bengal, and the Himalayan foothills, it is celebrated for its soft cadence, rich proverbs, and tea-garden agricultural life.

entities.title: Hindi
entities.subtitle: Indo-Aryan (Central group / Standard literary Hindustani) • Script: Devanagari
entities.description: Standard Hindi is the principal official language of the Government of Bihar, used in administration, the legislature, judiciary, education, and widespread journalism. Bihar is globally renowned as the birthplace of modern Hindi regional fiction, pioneering Hindi publishing houses, and monumental national poets.

entities.title: Madhubani / Mithila Painting
entities.subtitle: Mithila (Madhubani, Darbhanga, Sitamarhi) • Visual Folk Painting (GI Tagged)
entities.description: One of the world’s most celebrated folk art traditions, Mithila painting originated as a sacred mural art practiced exclusively by women in the domestic courtyards of the Mithila region. Traditionally painted on mud walls freshly coated with cow dung and clay, the art is characterized by double outlines filled with intricate hatching, stippling, and vibrant pigments extracted entirely from indigenous flora and minerals.
aliases: Centuries of mythological memory, sacred geometry, and female lineage painted with bamboo twigs.

typedAliases.value: Centuries of mythological memory, sacred geometry, and female lineage painted with bamboo twigs.

keywords: Handmade paper washed with cow dung and rice starch sizing
Split bamboo twigs (kalam) wrapped with raw cotton
Lampblack / soot (Kajal) for dense black outlines
Flame of the Forest (Palash/Kusum) flowers for crimson and ochre
Tussar silk fabric and pure cotton canvas
Sita Devi (Padma Shri 1981, pioneer of Bharni style)
Ganga Devi (Padma Shri 1984, National Award 1976, renowned for Kachni murals)
Baua Devi (Padma Shri 2017, master of mythic line drawings)
Dulari Devi (Padma Shri 2021, celebrated artist from the fishing community)

entities.title: Manjusha Art (Angika Snake Art)
entities.subtitle: Anga Region (Bhagalpur & Banka) • Narrative Box / Scroll Art (GI Tagged)
entities.description: Unique to the ancient Anga region (centered on modern Bhagalpur), Manjusha Art is an ancient sequential narrative folk painting tradition. Unlike other Indian folk arts that depict isolated mythological episodes, Manjusha is executed as a continuous, comic-strip style story that narrates the folklore of Behula, her steadfast love for husband Bala Lakhindar, and the worship of Mansa Devi (the serpent goddess Bishahari).
aliases: India’s only sequential scroll art in three sacred colors, telling the epic saga of Behula-Bishahari.

typedAliases.value: India’s only sequential scroll art in three sacred colors, telling the epic saga of Behula-Bishahari.

keywords: Pink pigment (representing love, devotion, and feminine strength)
Green pigment (representing vitality, poison, and nature)
Yellow pigment (representing intellect, divinity, and sacrifice)
Chakravarty Devi (Pioneering master artist who revived the endangered art)
Manoj Pandit (National & State awardee, master scroll illustrator)
Ulupi Jha (Eminent contemporary practitioner and trainer)
Anjana Keshri (Renowned artist and researcher of Angika folklore)

entities.title: Sujani Embroidery of Bihar
entities.subtitle: Tirhut (Muzaffarpur & Sitamarhi) • Textile Quilting & Needlework (GI Tagged)
entities.description: A deeply meditative textile tradition with a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, Sujani is practiced by rural women in Bihar’s Tirhut region. Derived from "Su" (pure / facilitating) and "Jani" (birth), the craft began as a domestic tradition of layering soft, discarded cotton saris and dhotis to create warm, quilted wraps for newborn babies, stitched with loving blessings and protective symbols.
aliases: Recycled vintage textiles stitched with rippled running threads into intimate diaries of women’s lives.

typedAliases.value: Recycled vintage textiles stitched with rippled running threads into intimate diaries of women’s lives.

keywords: Layered vintage cotton saris and dhotis (or pure Tussar silk for contemporary wall hangings)
Fine white quilting thread for background ripple effect
Colored cotton and silk embroidery threads (black, blue, crimson, ochre, forest green)
Nirmala Devi (National Award winner in traditional textile embroidery)
Sanju Devi (Master artisan and community trainer at Bhusra)
Sharda Devi (Pioneer in narrative social embroidery)
Artisan Collective of Mahila Vikas Samiti, Bhusra (Muzaffarpur)

entities.title: Sikki Grass Craft
entities.subtitle: Mithila & Tirhut (Madhubani, Darbhanga, Sitamarhi) • Natural Fibre Weaving & Basketry (GI Tagged)
entities.description: Sikki is the renowned golden grass craft of Northern Bihar. Sikki (Chrysopogon zizanioides) is a wild, fragrant reed with a natural metallic gold sheen that grows wild in the swampy river meadows of the Gandak and Kosi basins. In the hands of skilled women artisans, this humble wetland plant is split, dyed, and coiled around wild sweetgrass to produce sculptural baskets, ceremonial boxes (Pauti), animal figurines, and daily domestic utensils of remarkable tensile strength.
aliases: Golden wild wetland reeds split with teeth and coiled into sculptured, biodegradable vessels.

typedAliases.value: Golden wild wetland reeds split with teeth and coiled into sculptured, biodegradable vessels.

keywords: Wild Sikki grass (harvested during the autumn monsoon)
Munj / Khar grass (tough inner structural core)
Takua (traditional hand-forged iron needle with wooden handle)
Natural & food-grade dyes (scarlet red, sapphire blue, emerald green, golden-yellow)
Bindeshwari Devi (National Award winner in Sikki Basketry)
Shanti Devi (State Awardee, master sculptor of Sikki figurines)
Vimla Devi (Pioneering master artisan from Madhubani)
Krishna Kant Jha (Promoter of contemporary Sikki lighting and home decor)

entities.title: Bhagalpuri Tussar Silk Weaving
entities.subtitle: Anga Region (Bhagalpur & Banka) • Textile Handloom Weaving (GI Tagged)
entities.description: Known globally as the "Silk City" of India, Bhagalpur has been a world-renowned center of sericulture and handloom silk weaving for over two centuries. Bhagalpuri Tussar silk (often called "Kosa" silk) is wild forest silk spun from cocoons of the Antheraea paphia moth, which feed naturally on Asan and Arjun trees in the surrounding tribal forest belts. Prized for its rich porous texture, deep natural golden-beige luster, and remarkable thermal breathability, it holds a prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag.
aliases: The legendary "Queen of Wild Silks"—breathable, textured, and naturally golden on traditional pit looms.

typedAliases.value: The legendary "Queen of Wild Silks"—breathable, textured, and naturally golden on traditional pit looms.

keywords: Wild Tussar silk cocoons (Kosa) harvested from Arjun and Asan trees
Handspun Ghicha, Katia, and Matka silk yarns
Traditional wooden pit looms and fly-shuttles
Natural vegetable dyes (indigo, harda, lac, and madder) alongside eco-friendly azo-free dyes
Master Weavers of Nathnagar and Champanagar Cooperatives
Shri Mohammad Rafique (Eminent master weaver and recipient of National Handloom Award)
Weaver Collectives of Bhagalpur Regional Handloom Weavers Cooperative Union

entities.title: Tikuli Art of Patna
entities.hindiTitle: टिकुली कला (पटना की लघु तामचीनी कला)
entities.subtitle: Magadh (Patna) • Miniature Enamel & Lacquer Art
entities.description: Originating in the historic lanes of Patna City over 800 years ago, Tikuli art takes its name from "Tikli"—the ornate dot or bindi traditionally worn by Indian women between their eyebrows. Once crafted from micro-thin glass wafers adorned with pure 24-karat gold foil for royal queens and court dancers, Tikuli was reinvented in the modern era as an exquisite decorative plaque art rendered on enameled wood with sable-hair brushes.
aliases: An 800-year-old royal bindi tradition reincarnated on enameled wooden plaques with gold foil and sable brushes.

typedAliases.value: An 800-year-old royal bindi tradition reincarnated on enameled wooden plaques with gold foil and sable brushes.

keywords: High-density fiberboard (MDF) or seasoned wood panels
Zinc oxide, slate dust, and lacquer primer
Fine Japanese sable-hair and squirrel-tail brushes (Numbers 00 and 000)
Gold foil and imitation metallic leaf
Upendra Maharathi (Visionary artist and father of modern Bihar craft revival)
Ashok Kumar Biswas (State & National Award winner, trained thousands of women in Tikuli art)

entities.title: Kelwa Ke Paat Par (Ugeelan Surujmal)
entities.hindiTitle: केलवा के पात पर उगेलन सुरुजमल
entities.subtitle: Padma Bhushan Sharda Sinha • Chhath Mahaparva Solar Hymn (Bhojpuri)
entities.description: Composed with traditional acoustic dholak and harmonium, this classic rendition by Sharda Sinha captures the intimate domestic preparations of the vrati, awaiting dawn at the riverbank.

entities.title: Kaanch Hi Baans Ke Bahangiya
entities.subtitle: Padma Bhushan Sharda Sinha • Chhath Bamboo Offering Ballad (Bhojpuri)
entities.description: Reflects the central ecological spirit of Chhath: green bamboo woven by rural craft communities. The song expresses filial devotion, ritual sanctity, and familial solidarity.

entities.title: Mithila Vivah Geet: Samdaun (Bar Re Jatan Se Hum)
entities.hindiTitle: मिथिला समदौन: बड़ रे जतन से हम (बेटी विदाई गीत)
entities.subtitle: Padma Bhushan Sharda Sinha • Maithili Life-Cycle Bridal Farewell Ballad (Maithili)
entities.description: Passed down through generations of women in family courtyards, the Samdaun expresses the tender grief of farewell, honoring the daughter as Lakshmi of the maternal threshold.

entities.title: Jai Jai Bhairavi (Vidyapati Gosaunik Geet)
entities.hindiTitle: जय जय भैरवी असुर भयावनि (विद्यापति नचारी)
entities.subtitle: Padma Bhushan Sharda Sinha • Mahakavi Vidyapati Devotional Repertoire (Maithili)
entities.description: Set in Raag Bhairavi, this devotional song bridges Sanskrit classical metrics with vernacular Maithili devotional warmth. It opens major cultural assemblies in North Bihar.

entities.title: Darbhanga Dhrupad & Dhamar: Raag Gara
entities.hindiTitle: दरभंगा ध्रुपद एवं धमार: राग गारा
entities.subtitle: Pandit Ram Chatur Mallik • Gauhar Bani Classical Dhrupad Gharana (Hindustani Classical / Brajbhasha)
entities.description: Pt. Ram Chatur Mallik (1902–1990) was the premier court vocalist of the Darbhanga Raj and a Padma Shri recipient. His rendition adheres strictly to ancient Dhrupad-Dhamar canons.

entities.title: Dumraon Shehnai: Raag Bhairavi
entities.subtitle: Bharat Ratna Ustad Bismillah Khan • Dumraon Royal Court Shehnai Lineage (Instrumental)
entities.description: This signature Bhairavi recitation incorporates regional Purab Ang Thumri phrases and riverine folk inflections native to Western Bihar.

entities.title: Bhojpuri Bidesiya: Pyari Sundari Lokgeet
entities.subtitle: Dr. Nitu Kumari Nootan • Bhojpuri Folk Theatre (Bidesiya Naach) (Bhojpuri)
entities.description: Performed with expressive dramatic phrasing, harmonium, and dholak, voicing the longing and resilience of women left behind in village homes.

entities.title: Bhojpuri Kajari: Koyal Bin Bagiya Na Shobhe Raja
entities.hindiTitle: भोजपुरी कजरी: कोयल बिन बगिया ना शोभे राजा
entities.subtitle: Padma Bhushan Sharda Sinha • Monsoon Agrarian Folk Song (Kajari) (Bhojpuri)
entities.description: Characterized by swaying rhythmic cadences mirroring village rope swings (Jhula), celebrating nature’s revival and heartfelt domestic affection.

entities.title: Bhojpuri & Magahi Sohar Geet
entities.subtitle: Dr. Nitu Kumari Nootan • Childbirth Blessing Folk Tradition (Sohar) (Bhojpuri & Magahi)
entities.description: Accompanied by traditional dholak and metallic bronze plate (Thali) percussion, sung collectively in domestic courtyards without formal amplification.

entities.title: Kabir Nirgun: Hans Akela (Udd Jayega Hans Akela)
